extracted.intended_audience: early-career researchers preparing and submitting an ERC Starting Grant application (Principal Investigators)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation rules for preparing, submitting and being assessed for an ERC Starting Grant (early-career researcher Principal Investigator applying under Horizon Europe). Covers eligibility, host-institution requirements, application submission, evaluation (excellence), ranking, funding levels and the ethics review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: experience window since PhD
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers of any nationality with 2-7 years of experience since completion of PhD can apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The eligibility window is calculated from the relevant PhD date (see 'PhD defence date' rule). Extensions to this window are possible for specified reasons (maternity/paternity/parental leave, illness, national service, clinical training, natural disasters, asylum, victims of gender-based violence or any other form of violence) — consult the Parental leave webpage and the ERC Work Programme for specific rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific track record and research proposal quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must have a scientific track record showing great promise and submit an excellent research proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Starting Grant is for early-career scientists who have already produced excellent supervised work, are ready to work independently and show potential to be research leaders. The assessment weighs the excellence of both the research project and the Principal Investigator in conjunction (see 'excellence as sole criterion').

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of eligibility (acceptable reasons)
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligibility can be extended for reasons such as maternity, paternity, or parental leave, illness, national service, clinical training, natural disasters, asylum, or for victims of gender-based violence or any other form of violence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should check the Parental leave webpage and the latest ERC Work Programme to find the specific rules regarding how each reason is counted and documented for extending the eligibility window.

rubrics_metrics.name: PhD defence date as eligibility reference
rubrics_metrics.description: From 2023 the certified date of the successful PhD defence will be used as the reference point to calculate eligibility for Starting and Consolidator Grants instead of the date of award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This change aims to ensure fair competition across countries with different award practices. If no defence/viva was organised by the awarding institution, the applicant must provide written confirmation from that institution stating no defence/viva was organised and indicating the date when the PhD was approved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field of research: bottom-up (any field eligible)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications can be made in any field of research; the ERC's grants operate on a 'bottom-up' basis without predetermined priorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are no targeted thematic priorities; selection is based on excellence irrespective of scientific domain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host institution and location requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Research must be conducted in a public or private research organisation (host institution) located in one of the EU Member States or associated countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The host institution could be where the applicant already works or any other eligible legal entity in an EU Member State or associated country. The host must offer suitable conditions for the PI to independently lead the research and manage funding. The PI does not need to be employed by the host at submission time, but a mutual agreement/commitment is necessary if the proposal succeeds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single Principal Investigator submission requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications for an ERC grant require a single Principal Investigator to submit the application on behalf of their host institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ERC Starting Grant is awarded to an individual PI (not to multiple PIs); that individual is responsible for the proposal and, if successful, for leading the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team composition and permitted locations
rubrics_metrics.description: ERC grants support projects carried out by an individual researcher who can employ researchers of any nationality as team members; team members may be located in non-European countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vacancies for team members can be published on Euraxess-Jobs. Implementing Arrangements exist for hosting non-European scientists in ERC-funded teams; consult agreements for details on mobility and hosting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding amounts and eligible costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Starting Grants may be awarded up to €1.5 million for a period of 5 years (pro rata for shorter durations). An additional €1 million can be made available for further eligible costs when necessary; for PIs relocating from non-associated third countries additional funding may be up to €2 million.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for additional funding must be duly justified in the proposal. An ERC grant can cover up to 100% of total eligible direct costs plus a contribution of 25% of the total eligible costs towards indirect costs. Use the call documents for detailed eligible cost categories and justification expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application components and submission procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete ERC grant application must include administrative forms, the research proposal and supplementary documents, and be submitted by the specified closing date in response to a Call for Proposals via the EU submission service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calls are published on the ERC page, the EU Funding & Tenders Portal and in the Official Journal. Familiarise yourself with the EU submission service. You may update a submitted proposal any time before the deadline by submitting a new version (which overwrites the old one). Deadlines cannot be changed. You will receive an acknowledgement of receipt by e‑mail for each submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation principle: excellence as the sole criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals are evaluated on the basis of excellence as the sole criterion; this applies to the evaluation of both the research project and the Principal Investigator in conjunction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All eligible proposals are evaluated by external experts using excellence-based criteria; ensure both the project idea and the PI's track record and potential are presented clearly to demonstrate excellence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation panels, reviewers and domain structure
rubrics_metrics.description: For each call there are 28 panels covering sub-sections of three domains (Life Sciences LS; Physical and Engineering Sciences PE; Social Sciences and Humanities SH). Each panel consists of a chair and 10–16 members selected by the ERC Scientific Council; evaluations also rely on remote expert referees external to the panel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panel chairs' names are published before the deadline; panel members are published after the evaluation process concludes. Remote referees provide specialised expertise beyond the panel's generalist composition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring, quality threshold, ranking and budgetary cut-off
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer reviewers assess and score proposals; those who pass the quality threshold are ranked. Depending on the call budget, a budgetary cut-off applies to the ranking list and only the highest ranked proposals are offered an ERC grant until the call's budget has been used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand that passing the quality threshold does not guarantee funding; final funding depends on rank and available budget. Panels and reviewers follow the ERC scoring and ranking process — consult the Guide for peer reviewers for scoring details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics review: requirement, basis and stages
rubrics_metrics.description: If your proposal is selected for funding it will undergo an ethics review (legal requirement under Horizon Europe Regulation 2021/695). The basis for the ethics review is Part A (including the Ethics Issues Table – EIT – and the Ethics Self-Assessment – ESA) and Part B of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A well-detailed ESA is crucial to facilitate the process as it clarifies what issues are linked to the proposed activities and how they will be dealt with. The ethics review comprises three stages: (1) Ethics pre-screening by ERCEA staff to clear proposals without ethics issues or with simple issues; (2) Ethics screening by panels of independent ethics reviewers to identify proposals with potentially Serious and/or Complex ethics issues — clearance of non-Serious/Complex issues can include observations and references to documents to be kept on file; after screening applicants might be contacted (typically one week after the screening panel) and given 3 weeks to reply; (3) Ethics assessment by panels of independent ethics reviewers for discussion of Serious and/or Complex issues, which can lead to ethics deliverables or follow-up during project implementation. Research involving human embryonic stem cells (hESCs) requires all steps and an additional EC approval following the comitology procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical preparatory steps and applicant support
rubrics_metrics.description: Before the call is published: find which ERC grant and call is suitable; identify host institution and team; contact your National Contact Point (NCP). Once the call is open: read call documents, contact host and gather details, start writing, allow time for others to review your draft, familiarise yourself with the EU submission service, and submit as early as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use NCP support, peers and scientists for feedback. Watch ERC instructional videos on starting, writing the proposal, understanding evaluation, preparing for interview, and ethics to better prepare. Deadlines cannot be changed — plan time for internal review and administrative coordination with the host institution.
